content: 1. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) taken orally twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) taken orally twice daily. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) decrease the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of Viekira Pak with darunavir/ritonavir is not recommended. 13. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease clearance of ondansetron. However, no dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased HIV viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 18. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Reduce the dose of osilodrostat, a CYP3A4 substrate, by half when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no other alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient more closely for adverse effects. 22. Darunavir increases the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative anticonvulsant or antiretroviral therapy to avoid potential changes in exposures. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response. 26. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required.
